verses.text: This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah about the drought:
"Judah mourns. Its towns are dying. Its people sit on the ground in mourning. A cry goes up from Jerusalem.
The nobles send their servants for water. They go to the wells but find no water. They come back with empty jars. Ashamed and confused, they cover their heads.
The ground is cracked because there has been no rain in the land. The farmers are upset and cover their heads.
Even the deer in the field leaves her newborn fawn, because there is no grass.
Wild donkeys stand on the bare hills, panting like jackals. Their eyes grow dim because there is no food to eat."
Even though our sins accuse us, LORD, do something for the sake of your name. We have turned away from you many times. We have sinned against you.
You are the hope of Israel, its Savior in times of trouble. Why are you like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who stays only one night?
Why are you like someone who is confused, like a warrior who cannot save anyone? You are among us, LORD, and we are called by your name. Do not leave us!

This is what the LORD says about this people: "They love to wander. They do not hold back their feet. So the LORD does not accept them. Now he will remember their wrongdoing and punish them for their sins."
Then the LORD said to me, "Do not pray for good things for these people.
When they fast, I will not listen to their cry. When they offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. Instead, I will destroy them with war, hunger, and disease."
But I said, "Oh, Lord GOD! Look, the prophets keep telling them, 'You will not see war or hunger. I will give you lasting peace in this place.'"

Then the LORD said to me, "The prophets are prophesying lies in my name. I did not send them or command them or speak to them. They are prophesying to you false visions, fortune telling, worthless ideas, and lies from their own minds.

So this is what the LORD says about the prophets who are prophesying in my name, though I did not send them, who say, 'No war or hunger will touch this land.' Those same prophets will die by war and hunger.

And the people they are prophesying to will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem, killed by hunger and war. There will be no one to bury them, or their wives, sons, or daughters. I will pour out on them the punishment their wickedness deserves.
Speak this word to them: 'Let my eyes overflow with tears night and day without stopping. For my people, my virgin daughter, have been struck with a crushing blow, a terrible wound.
If I go out into the countryside, I see those killed by the sword. If I go into the city, I see those dying of hunger. Both prophets and priests wander through a land they do not know.'"

Have you completely rejected Judah? Do you hate Zion? Why have you struck us so badly that we cannot be healed? We hoped for peace, but nothing good came. We hoped for a time of healing, but there was only terror.
LORD, we admit our wickedness and the sins of our ancestors. We have sinned against you.
For the sake of your name, do not reject us. Do not disgrace your glorious throne. Remember your covenant with us and do not break it.
Can any of the worthless idols of the nations bring rain? Can the sky send showers by itself? No, it is you, LORD our God! So we put our hope in you, for you are the one who does all these things.
